title: Telemetry bootstrap plan for feature rollouts
body:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic bootstrap plan for telemetry that teams can copy when they roll a new feature or model variant. Goal is to get a minimal set of reliable metrics + traces + dashboard widgets live within one sprint so product/SEs have immediate visibility and we can iterate.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to new serving routes, rollout toggles, and model swaps across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Not a comprehensive instrumentation spec; this is the minimum observability surface for production readiness.
- We prioritize signals that help: (1) detect degraded latency/cost, (2) catch correctness regressions tied to model changes, (3) enable quick RCA within 30m.

Quick checklist (bootstrap template):
1) Define 6 core metrics to emit (see definitions below).
2) Add a lightweight trace span for request -> router -> model-executor -> cache-check.
3) Create 3 dashboard widgets: latency quantiles, error-rate by upstream, and anomalous token-cost heatmap.
4) Wire alerting on SLI thresholds (P95 latency, error rate > X, token-cost delta > Y%).
5) Add rollout tags to traces and metrics (rollout_id, model_version, route_tag).

Core metric definitions (emit at request granularity unless noted):
- request_count: counter of incoming requests to the route. Tag by route, customer_tier, rollout_id. (unit: count)
- request_success: counter where response HTTP/streaming completed with non-error closure. useful for percent-success. (unit: count)
- latency_ms: histogram of end-to-end wall clock from request arrival to response last-byte. Buckets: 0-10,10-25,25-50,50-100,100-250,250-500,500-1000,>1000. Tag by route, model_variant. (unit: ms)
- model_infer_ms: histogram of time spent in model execution (excludes router, network, and kv-cache hits). Tag by instance_type, quantization_profile.
- kv_cache_hit: counter with labels {hit|miss} and kv_key_prefix. Important for cost SLOs and to tune TTL.
- token_cost_units: gauge that estimates billed token units per request (use same calc as billing pipeline). Emit per-request and aggregate daily.

Tracing basics (span plan):
- trace root: request-received (tags: request_id, user_id?, route, rollout_id)
  - span: router-dispatch (time in routing layer & policy eval)
    - span: prefix-cache-lookup (indicate hit/miss; attach cached_bytes)
    - span: model-proxy (network costs, queue wait)
      - span: model-executor (embed model_variant, instance_id, sequence_length)
- Attach lightweight annotations: model_variant_rollout (boolean), fallback_reason (if any), token_estimate.
- Sampling: for initial rollout, keep traces for 10% of successful requests + 100% of errored requests. Increase sampling to 50% during active canary windows.

Dashboard widget suggestions (compact page layout):
Top row (overview):
- [W1] Rolling key numbers: request_count (1d), request_success%, P95 latency, avg token_cost_units.
- [W2] Latency heatmap split by model_variant / rollout_id (bucketed by latency_ms).
Second row (investigation):
- [W3] Error waterfall: error_type vs route vs recent traces (links into trace UI).
- [W4] KV cache hit ratio by prefix + trend (7d).
Bottom row (cost & regression):
- [W5] Token-cost delta: compare current model_variant to previous baseline (7d median).
- [W6] Request-level scatter: model_infer_ms vs token_cost_units colored by instance_type.
Notes: each widget must be filterable by rollout_id and environment (prod/staging). Keep panel query windows short (5m/1h/24h) as appropriate.

Alerting and SLOs (starter):
- SLO1 latency_p95 < 400ms for small routes; separate buckets for long-running batched routes. Alert if breached for 5m with support paging.
- SLO2 error_rate < 0.5% (5m). Alert on sudden step-ups > 3x baseline.
- SLO3 token_cost anomaly: trigger if median token_cost_units for variant deviates by > 20% vs baseline for >= 30m.
- Pager escalation: alerts on SLO1/SLO2 are paged; cost anomalies create tickets (ops + product).

Investigation playbook (first 20 minutes):
1) Check W1 for global context (requests per min, P95).
2) Narrow by rollout_id and correlate with W2/W4; if cache_hit dropped, suspect TTL/invalidations.
3) If latency spike, open trace for recent errored and slow traces; look at model-executor span durations and queue wait.
4) If token-cost delta high, compare prompts/inputs in sampled traces and check inference config (temperature, stop tokens, max_tokens param).
5) Triage to model, infra, or routing. Create RCA ticket and attach trace links and a pinboard screenshot.

Sampling and cost tradeoffs (practical rules):
- Keep base trace sampling low (10%) to limit storage, escalate during canaries to 50-100% for a short window (2–24h).
- For high-volume routes, use head-sampling for errors: keep 100% of non-200 responses.
- Lease metrics gateway quotas per team: metrics with cardinality > 1k per minute need design review.

Rollout instrumentation timeline (example sprint):
Day 0: instrumentation PR merged (metrics + span annotations + rollout tags).
Day 1: smoke deploy to staging, sanity dashboards for W1/W2; team signoff.
Day 2–3: begin canary (5% traffic), set canary-level alert thresholds, increase trace sampling.
Day 4–7: gradual ramp to 100% if SLOs hold. Keep enhanced telemetry for 72h after 100% before scaling down traces.

Open questions / tradeoffs (to resolve in review):
- token_cost_units calc parity: should we emit billing-estimate or raw token-count? Which makes downstream alerts simpler?
- Label cardinality: how many model_variant labels are reasonable? prefer version aliasing to long sha strings.
- KV cache instrumentation detail level: prefix vs prompt-fingerprint. Storing fingerprint may be sensitive.

To-dos (owners and next actions):
- Ethan: add rollout_id tag to router and ensure it surfaces to traces (due: 2025-11-21).
- Maya: PR for metric names & histogram buckets in runtime (due: 2025-11-18).
- Jamal: dashboard skeleton + widget queries (due: 2025-11-22).
- Sofia: write alert runbook snippets and oncall escalation (due: 2025-11-25).

Notes to self: keep this doc small and reusable. Copy into feature repo README as OBS-bootstrapping.md when feature is ready.

References & links:

- Example PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/512
- Canaries: see OBS-421 for previous canary thresholds and dataset.
